question: For a curve with an advisory speed of 40 mph and a radius within 401 to 700 feet, what Chevron Alignment sign spacing and placement are indicated?
model_answer: Direct Answer: For a curve with a 40-mph advisory speed and a radius in the 401 to 700 feet range, Table 2C-5 indicates a Chevron Alignment (W1-8) sign spacing of 120 feet, measured from the point of curvature (PC). Placement-wise, the chevrons must be installed on the outside of the curve, in line with and at approximately a right angle to approaching traffic, at a minimum mounting height of 4 feet. Standards (mandatory): - "If used, Chevron Alignment signs shall be installed on the outside of a turn or curve, in line with and at approximately a right angle to approaching traffic. Chevron Alignment signs shall be installed at a minimum height of 4 feet, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the traveled way." Guidance (recommended): - The approximate spacing of Chevron Alignment signs on the turn or curve, measured from the point of curvature (PC), should be as shown in Table 2C-5. For an advisory speed of 35 to 45 mph and a curve radius of 401 to 700 feet, the table shows a sign spacing of 120 feet. Options (permitted): - Chevron Alignment signs may be used instead of or in addition to standard delineators (per Chapter 3G / Section 2C.08 cross-reference in the figure notes). Visual evidence: [Image 1] Table 2C-5 shows the row "35 to 45 mph" advisory speed / "401 to 700 feet" curve radius corresponding to "120 feet" sign spacing, with a note that the radius–advisory speed relationship should not be used to determine the advisory speed. [Image 2] Figure 2C-2 (Sheet 1 of 2, A – Curve) illustrates W1-8L/W1-8R chevrons placed on the outside of the curve facing approaching traffic, with Note 3 directing users to Table 2C-5 for spacing of W1-8 signs. [Image 4] The full-page view of Section 2C.08 confirms the Standard for outside-of-curve placement at a right angle to traffic and 4-foot minimum height, plus the Guidance referencing Table 2C-5. [Image 5] Figure 2C-2 (Revision 1 version) similarly depicts chevron placement along the outside of the curve. [Image 3] Page 154 lists Chevron Alignment (W1-8) signs among treatments for changes in horizontal alignment (see Section 2C.08). [Image 6] Figure 3G-1 notes that Chevron Alignment signs (W1-8) may be used instead of or in addition to standard delineators. Citations: - Table 2C-5 (p.158) - Section 2C.08 Guidance §5 (p.158) - Section 2C.08 Standard §4 (p.158) - Figure 2C-2 (p.156) - Section 2C.05 Support §2 (p.154)
gold_answer: Typical spacing is 120 feet. The signs must be on the outside of the curve, approximately at right angles to approaching traffic, with a minimum mounting height of 4 feet.
